newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil up while regrade falters.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil up while regrade falters.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices continued to be sustained at firm levels as the swaps jet fuel/gas oil regrade widened further, traders said on Wednesday.
The firm gas oil market seen in March and April is now expected to spill over into May as buying interest from a Singapore trader appeared to be maintained at over $27.00 per barrel, traders said.
They noted that current spot prices are about $2.00 per barrel more than during the same period last year.

Earlier expectations that most of the arbitrage cargoes from the West would be placed in Hong Kong has not materialised as sellers preferred to sell in Singapore, where they were getting better fixed-priced sales, traders said.

"It makes better value to sell them here," one trader said. "Over here, you can do a fixed priced deal, you know your cost and you know your margins. If you sell to China you face a lot of operational headaches."

But traders said the storage tanks in Hong Kong are now at a "manageable level" and no longer at very low levels as seen during mid-March. They said there has been a few enquiries into Hong Kong, with the latest bid for a part cargo at $1.40 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes, cost-and-freight basis.

In Singapore, a local trader was bidding at $27.40 for April 20-24 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis, facing an offer from a Swiss trader. Other offers were seen from a US trader and a European major between $27.20 and $27.45 per barrel.
Jet fuel was offered 70 cents higher at $26.00 with no bid seen.

Traders said swaps jet/gas oil regrade continued to be battered as demand for jet was expected to remain in the doldrums with April seen at minus 95/70 cents per barrel, compared with Tuesday's minus 60/40 cents.

Taiwan bought one 32,000-tonne cargo of jet fuel for end-May arrival in a tender at below $204 per tonne from a South Korean refiner, c-and-f basis. This was about $10 per tonne below Taiwan's last purchase for April arrival.
Nepal's tender for diesel attracted a low offer of $194 per tonne, c-and-f from Glencore and $204 per tonne for kerosene from Mitsubishi Corp.
